Eve (sec-eng): FYI, SCIM push to acme-corp is spiking errors and creating duplicate users. Started right after their SSO rotation ~09:12 UTC.
Tom (infra): Ugh. Any server logs or error ids?
Eve (sec-eng): Pasted a snippet from the SCIM worker:
```
2026-03-19T09:12:34Z ERROR scim/worker.go:178 user create conflict (external_id=acme|john.doe): 409 DuplicateResource
2026-03-19T09:12:34Z WARN auth/saml: Assertion InResponseTo mismatch: expected='_abc123' got='_def456'
2026-03-19T09:12:34Z ERROR kms/sign: failed verify signature: key not found (key-id=projects/redwood/keys/idp-sign-rot)
```
Nadia (oncall): @Eve can you confirm whether this is happening for all users or a subset?
Eve (sec-eng): Appears for users with long federated usernames (emails with long subdomains) and any user created in the last 24h. Also saw some RBAC mapping failures — roles not attached after provisioning.
Luis (platform): The KMS error stands out. We recently accepted a key rollover from the IdP last night. If the old key is gone, signature verify can fail and our SAML library could be treating the assertion as replayed or malformed.
Sam (devex): Could also be NameID format changes. Some IdPs switch NameID from email to transient/opaque which we use as external_id in SCIM. If NameID length > our external_id limit we might truncate and produce duplicates.
Asha (compliance): If external_ids are changing we need to audit every change — this touches our audit log requirements. Please keep an immutable record of the pre/post mappings.
Tom (infra): Quick checks: 1) Can we fetch the IdP metadata and confirm current signing cert thumbprint? 2) Check our KMS key aliases for the previous key. 3) Look at recent SCIM job payloads for external_id values.
Eve (sec-eng): I downloaded the IdP metadata and the signing cert fingerprint changed. The IdP uploaded a new cert but didn't keep the old one online. We have the old cert in a backup snapshot but the key alias in KMS rotated.
Nadia (oncall): Rolling back to previous known-good config may be fastest. @Tom can infra re-add old cert alias to KMS and re-deploy the verifier?
Tom (infra): I can restore the old key alias from the snapshot to staging now and run a smoke SCIM push. ETA 15m.
idp-bot: Automatic alert: IdP metadata changed for acme-corp at 2026-03-19T09:10:21Z. New cert SHA256=9a:bb:cc:... Previous cert archived.
Luis (platform): If we re-enable the old cert, we should also ensure our SAML parser doesn't silently truncate NameIDs. I'm opening a small patch to validate external_id length and reject short/ambiguous mappings.
Sam (devex): For customers using transient NameIDs we should map on eduPersonPrincipalName or an attribute claim if present, not just NameID. Add that to the troubleshooting checklist.
Eve (sec-eng): Also found RBAC mapping logs showing failed role assignment: "role attach failed: user not found (scim_id=null)" — likely because SCIM create returned a 409 and we retried create instead of reconcile.
Asha (compliance): Capture all retried operations in the audit trail. Retries that changed state must be visible to auditors.
Tom (infra): Staging restore looks good: SCIM push succeeded against staging with old key alias restored. I'll promote to prod after we confirm no side effects.
Nadia (oncall): Recommend canary: run provisioning for 5 orgs in prod with old cert restored, monitor for duplicates and RBAC regressions for 30m. If green, roll to everyone.
Eve (sec-eng): Agreed. I'll enable extra logging for external_id and NameID claim, and log the exact assertion fingerprint before verification.
Luis (platform): I'll ship the small validation patch to reject truncated external_ids and log the raw claim so we can audit collisions.
Sam (devex): I'll post a short KB for support: "If your IdP rotates certs and users see duplicates, check NameID format, external_id length and ensure old certs are accessible for key rollover window."
Asha (compliance): Keep me updated with the canary results and provide the audit dump for the affected window once the canary completes.
Eve (sec-eng): Can we also add an automated alert: if SCIM create returns 409 and external_id collisions > 3 within 1m, trigger an incident? That would catch regressions.
Tom (infra): Yes, I'll add an alert rule to paging config after canary.
Nadia (oncall): Can I get explicit rollback playbook steps in the thread? If canary fails I need clear steps to revert.
Eve (sec-eng): Rollback playbook (short):
1) Re-add previous cert alias to KMS (or restore snapshot).
2) Restart saml-verifier service.
3) Run scoped SCIM reconciliation for affected orgs: `POST /_admin/scim/reconcile?org=acme-corp`
4) Monitor audit logs for duplicates; if duplicates created, run dedupe script `tools/scim/dedupe --org acme-corp --dry-run` then `--apply`
5) Notify compliance and affected customers.
Sam (devex): I'll put the playbook into the runbook doc and link from the KB.
Eve (sec-eng): Thanks all — running the canary now and will report back in ~40m. :thumbsup:
